questions.stem: The normal GESTATION period (pregnancy duration) in humans is:

options.option_text: ~40 weeks (~280 days, 9 months) from last menstrual period

questions.explanation: Normal HUMAN GESTATION: ~40 WEEKS (280 days, approximately 9 months) calculated from the first day of the LAST MENSTRUAL PERIOD (LMP) — conventionally used by doctors. Actual FERTILISATION occurs ~2 weeks after LMP (so true embryonic development is ~38 weeks). DIVIDED into 3 TRIMESTERS: 1st trimester (1-12 weeks) — organogenesis, high miscarriage risk; 2nd (13-28 weeks) — growth, fetal movements felt; 3rd (29-40 weeks) — rapid weight gain, lung maturation. PRETERM: before 37 weeks. TERM: 37-42 weeks. POSTTERM: after 42 weeks (needs induction). LABOUR: 3 stages — (1) dilation of cervix (up to 10cm); (2) delivery of baby; (3) delivery of placenta. OTHER ANIMAL GESTATION periods: Elephant ~22 months (longest among mammals), whales ~10-17 months, horses 11 months, cows 9 months, dogs ~63 days, cats ~65 days, rabbits ~31 days, hamsters ~16 days (shortest among mammals). Record: opossum ~12 days (briefest pregnancy in mammals). PLATYPUS — lays eggs despite being a mammal (monotreme). HUMAN MENSTRUAL CYCLE: ~28 days; ovulation around day 14; egg viable ~24 hours; sperm viable in female body ~3-5 days.

questions.stem: FERTILISATION (fusion of sperm + egg) typically occurs in which part of the female reproductive tract?

options.option_text: FALLOPIAN TUBE (oviduct — ampulla region) ~24-48 hours after ovulation

questions.explanation: FERTILISATION occurs in the FALLOPIAN TUBE (oviduct), specifically in the AMPULLA region (widest part, near the ovary). AFTER OVULATION, egg is picked up by fimbriae of fallopian tube → travels toward uterus via peristalsis + cilia. SPERM (deposited in vagina) swim UP through cervix → uterus → fallopian tube (~30 min to 12 hours to reach egg, only ~300 of 200-500 million make it there). Fusion ('syngamy'): sperm penetrates egg → zygote. Cleavage (repeated mitotic divisions) starts. 4-5 days later: BLASTOCYST arrives at uterus + IMPLANTS in endometrium (~day 6-10 after fertilisation). ECTOPIC PREGNANCY: implantation in fallopian tube (emergency — can rupture, 95% of ectopics are tubal); other sites — ovary, cervix, abdomen. DIAGNOSED by ultrasound + hCG levels. TREATMENT: methotrexate or surgery. IVF: fertilisation happens in vitro (in petri dish); first IVF baby LOUISE BROWN, UK, 1978. India's first IVF baby: Durga / Kanupriya Agarwal, Kolkata, 1978 (by Dr Subhas Mukhopadhyay). 25 July observed as WORLD IVF DAY.

questions.stem: Which PAIR of chromosomes determines SEX in humans?

options.option_text: The 23rd pair: XX = female, XY = male

questions.explanation: Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes: 22 pairs of AUTOSOMES + 1 pair of SEX CHROMOSOMES. SEX CHROMOSOMES: X (large, ~155 Mbp, 800+ genes) and Y (small, ~59 Mbp, <100 genes). FEMALE = XX (two X chromosomes, both inherited from parents). MALE = XY (one X from mother + one Y from father). SEX DETERMINED BY THE SPERM — father contributes either X (→ XX daughter) or Y (→ XY son). The Y chromosome carries the SRY GENE (Sex-determining Region Y), which triggers testes development in the embryo ~6-8 weeks after conception. Without SRY, ovaries develop by default. OTHER SEX-DETERMINATION SYSTEMS in nature: Birds + some reptiles: ZW system — FEMALES are ZW (heterogametic), males ZZ. Insects/grasshoppers: XO (male = X only, female = XX). Bees/wasps: HAPLODIPLOIDY — males from unfertilised eggs (haploid), females from fertilised (diploid). Crocodiles + some turtles: TEMPERATURE-DEPENDENT (TSD) — no sex chromosomes; egg incubation temperature determines sex. Humans have AMELOGENIN gene on both X + Y — used for forensic sex determination via PCR.

questions.stem: The female reproductive hormone produced by the OVARIES (stimulates uterine lining, secondary sexual characters) is:
questions.explanation: FEMALE SEX HORMONES: (1) ESTROGEN — three forms — ESTRADIOL (main in reproductive years), ESTRIOL (pregnancy), ESTRONE (post-menopausal). Produced mainly by OVARIES (granulosa cells of follicles) + placenta during pregnancy + adrenal glands in small amounts. Functions: develops female secondary sexual characters (breasts, wider hips, body fat distribution), matures reproductive tract, regulates menstrual cycle (first half — proliferative phase), bone health, cardiovascular protection. (2) PROGESTERONE — secreted mainly by CORPUS LUTEUM (after ovulation) + placenta during pregnancy. Maintains endometrium (pregnancy lining), inhibits uterine contractions early in pregnancy. Levels high in 2nd half of cycle (secretory/luteal phase). MALE SEX HORMONE: TESTOSTERONE (androgen) — produced by LEYDIG cells of TESTES + adrenals (small amounts in women too). Secondary male characters (muscle mass, facial hair, deep voice), sperm production. HYPOTHALAMIC-PITUITARY-GONADAL (HPG) AXIS: Hypothalamus → GnRH → Pituitary → LH + FSH → Gonads → sex hormones. Feedback loop regulates all stages. MENOPAUSE (~45-55 years in women) — estrogen drops → bone loss, hot flushes, mood changes. primary female sex hormones.

questions.stem: Which hormone is detected by PREGNANCY TESTS (both urine strips and blood tests)?
questions.explanation: hCG (HUMAN CHORIONIC GONADOTROPIN) — the 'pregnancy hormone'. Produced by the PLACENTA (specifically trophoblast cells of the implanted embryo) starting from about day 6-8 post-fertilisation. DETECTED in urine by ~10-14 days after conception (a few days after missed period — commercial urine tests are ~97% accurate by then). Blood tests can detect earlier (~8-9 days post-ovulation). Peaks around 8-11 weeks of pregnancy, then gradually declines. Function in pregnancy: maintains the CORPUS LUTEUM of ovary, which continues secreting progesterone till the placenta takes over (~8-12 weeks). Clinical uses of hCG: confirming pregnancy, diagnosing ectopic pregnancy (abnormally low/rising hCG), miscarriage monitoring, gestational trophoblastic disease (very high hCG), testicular cancer diagnosis (men). Also used (controversially) for weight loss diets — INEFFECTIVE + FDA-disapproved. Commercial pregnancy tests use MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (via ELISA — Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay) to detect β-hCG. First commercially available urine pregnancy test: 1976. Before that: rabbit test (inject woman's urine into rabbit — if rabbit's ovaries enlarged, positive — cruel + slow).

questions.stem: The MENSTRUAL CYCLE lasts an average of 28 days. OVULATION (release of egg from ovary) typically occurs on approximately:
questions.explanation: MENSTRUAL CYCLE phases (28-day typical, but varies 21-35 days): (1) MENSTRUAL PHASE (Days 1-5) — uterine lining (endometrium) sheds if no pregnancy. Bleeding ~30-80 mL. (2) FOLLICULAR / PROLIFERATIVE PHASE (Days 1-13) — FSH stimulates ovarian follicles; one dominates → Graafian follicle. Endometrium rebuilds under estrogen. (3) OVULATION (Day ~14) — triggered by LH SURGE (from pituitary). Egg released. ~1 egg per cycle. Viable ~24 hours. Fertile window ~5 days before + 1 day after ovulation. (4) LUTEAL / SECRETORY PHASE (Days 15-28) — ruptured follicle → CORPUS LUTEUM → progesterone. Endometrium thickens. If fertilisation: hCG maintains CL → pregnancy. If not: CL regresses → progesterone falls → menstruation. CYCLE REGULATED BY: Hypothalamus → GnRH → Pituitary → LH + FSH → Ovaries → Estrogen + Progesterone → feedback to H + P. FIRST period = MENARCHE (~12-13 years typically). LAST period = MENOPAUSE (~45-55 years). PMS (Premenstrual Syndrome) — hormone-related mood/physical symptoms days before periods. PCOS (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome) — common cause of irregular periods, infertility; associated with insulin resistance.

questions.stem: The PLACENTA — temporary organ that connects mother + fetus during pregnancy — primarily facilitates:

options.option_text: Exchange of OXYGEN, CO₂, nutrients, waste + hormones
Digestion of food for the baby

questions.explanation: PLACENTA — temporary organ developed during pregnancy. Formed from trophoblast cells of embryo + maternal tissues. Attached to UTERINE WALL via CHORIONIC VILLI. CONNECTED to fetus by UMBILICAL CORD (2 arteries + 1 vein). FUNCTIONS: (1) RESPIRATION — O₂ from mother → fetus; CO₂ reverse (fetus uses mother's lungs essentially). (2) NUTRITION — glucose, amino acids, vitamins, minerals diffuse maternal → fetal. (3) EXCRETION — fetal urea + waste → maternal circulation. (4) PROTECTION — placental 'barrier' filters many (not all) harmful substances + pathogens. Some pathogens cross (TORCH infections — Toxoplasma, Rubella, CMV, Herpes, syphilis, Zika). Most drugs cross. (5) HORMONE PRODUCTION — hCG, estrogen, progesterone, hPL. (6) IMMUNOLOGY — passive IgG transfer provides infant immunity for ~6 months. Maternal + fetal blood NEVER MIX (separated by placental membranes). Umbilical VEIN carries OXYGENATED blood (fetus→mother direction is reversed from typical vein-artery naming). Placenta typically weighs ~500g at term. Delivered as 'afterbirth' in third stage of labour. PLACENTA PREVIA (placenta covers cervix) + PLACENTAL ABRUPTION — serious complications. but NO mixing of maternal + fetal blood.

questions.stem: IDENTICAL (MONOZYGOTIC) TWINS differ from FRATERNAL (DIZYGOTIC) TWINS in that identical twins:

options.option_text: Develop from the SAME zygote that splits → 100% identical DNA; always same sex
Develop from two separate eggs fertilised by two sperm

questions.explanation: TWINS come in two types: (1) IDENTICAL / MONOZYGOTIC TWINS (MZ) — ONE sperm fertilises ONE egg → zygote splits in early development (day 2-8) → 2 embryos. 100% identical DNA. ALWAYS same sex. ~3-4 per 1000 births globally (rate fairly constant across populations). Can share placenta (monochorionic) or not (dichorionic) — depending on when split happens. (2) FRATERNAL / DIZYGOTIC TWINS (DZ) — TWO eggs released + fertilised by TWO sperm → 2 zygotes develop together. ~50% shared DNA (like regular siblings). Can be SAME SEX or OPPOSITE SEX. Rate varies: ~6/1000 globally, higher in certain populations (West Africa ~20/1000, Nigeria's Yoruba people have highest twin rate), lower in Asia (~4/1000 including India). Family history + fertility treatments increase DZ rate. CONJOINED ('Siamese') TWINS — rare MZ twins where split was INCOMPLETE, stuck together. Chang + Eng Bunker (1811-1874) from Siam, touring 'curiosities' gave 'Siamese twins' their name. Modern surgical separation sometimes possible. POLAR BODY TWINS — rare, egg + its polar body each fertilised. MIRROR TWINS — MZ with opposite-handed features.

questions.stem: PUBERTY in girls typically begins between ages:
questions.explanation: PUBERTY — biological transition from childhood to reproductive adulthood. GIRLS: typically starts 8-13 years. Sequence: (1) THELARCHE (breast development, age ~10); (2) PUBARCHE (pubic hair, age ~11); (3) Growth spurt (~11-12); (4) MENARCHE (first period, avg 12-13 years globally; ~13 in India historically, now ~11-12 due to better nutrition); (5) Completion of pubertal changes ~15-17. BOYS: 9-14 years start. Sequence: (1) testicular enlargement (first sign); (2) penile growth; (3) pubic hair; (4) growth spurt (~13-14); (5) voice deepening + facial hair; (6) spermarche (first sperm production). HORMONES DRIVING PUBERTY: hypothalamic GnRH pulsatility → pituitary LH+FSH → gonadal sex hormones (estrogen in girls, testosterone in boys) + adrenal androgens (both sexes — pubic/axillary hair). PRECOCIOUS PUBERTY: before 8 (girls) / 9 (boys) — medical concern. DELAYED PUBERTY: no signs by 13 (girls) / 14 (boys) — workup needed. Globally, age of puberty DECREASING over past 150 years (better nutrition — secular trend). Menarche used to be ~17 in 1800s Europe; ~12-13 now. TANNER STAGES (1-5) used by doctors to track pubertal progression. EMOTIONAL/COGNITIVE changes also significant — brain still developing into early 20s. with MENARCHE — first period — around 12-13 years average.
